title: .revloop.json
description: Project configuration for revloop. It is read from .revloop/config.json when that file exists, and otherwise from .revloop.json at the repository root; the two are never merged. Every field is optional, and anything absent is detected, takes a built-in default, or takes the --rigor level's value, and the step 1 table shows which in its source column. Reviewers are not defined here; see schema/reviewer.schema.json.

version.description: Config format version. An unknown major version aborts rather than degrading.

baseBranch.description: Null or absent: read from gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef.

branchPrefixes.description: Absent: derived from the repository's own commit subjects.

verify.description: Commands run before pushing. They are printed in the step 1 table before they run and are never pre-approved.

verifyNotes.description: What CI runs that the verify commands do not, if anything.

verifiedLabel.description: Label introducing the list of commands actually run, e.g. "Verified:".

trailers.description: {model} expands to the name of the model running the loop. It is not {reviewModel}, the model a local review runs on.

pr.description: The merge method is not configurable: the loop always creates a merge commit. The CI check before a merge is not configurable either.

defaults.description: Defaults for the command flags. A flag always overrides its default. --merge, --auto, --rigor and --config have no key: this file comes from the repository you are working in, so it cannot turn on merging, remove a confirmation, lower the review bar or choose the reviewer. --model has none because its value is interpolated into a command line, and --no-publish has none because nobody has asked for one.

maxRounds.description: Round cap for the remote commands. The order is --max-rounds, then this key, then the number the --rigor level supplies (5 at the default, standard).

localMaxRounds.description: Round cap for the local commands. The order is --max-rounds, then this key, then the number the --rigor level supplies (3 at the default, standard).
